config.documentTitleFull: WRITTEN REQUEST TO A NON-COURT RECORD HOLDER TO CONFORM ITS RECORDS TO AN AUTOMATIC EXPUNCTION UNDER G.S. 15A-146(a4)

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Charges expunged by operation of law under G.S. 15A-146(a4): the clerk is not required to transmit an expunction order to other entities, so an agency that still holds and disseminates the charge may be unaware the expunction occurred.
States the notification scheme for expunctions generally.
Restores the person to the status they occupied before the arrest, charge or conviction.
The court record itself is the clerk's and the AOC's to maintain; this request does not reach it.

verificationStatute.description: The participant signs and dates the request themselves; no wet-signature rule applies and notarization is not required. The agency simply needs an identifiable, signed request.

counselFlags: This is correspondence, not a filing: nothing is filed with a court, no court, prosecutor or opposing party receives notice, and no service rule applies.

The letter must not assert that the agency has broken any duty, and it must not certify that the expunction occurred; it states the participant's account and the statutory basis and asks the holder to check its own records.
Open counsel question (registry): is AOC-G-260 the correct instrument for evidencing an automatic expunction under G.S. 15A-146(a4) to a non-court record holder, and if not, what is?

Open counsel question (registry): does any North Carolina statute or rule oblige a non-court record holder to conform its records once it has notice of an automatic expunction under G.S. 15A-146(a4)? Until resolved the letter asks and does not demand.

This action presupposes the automatic expunction occurred; where it did not run, the petition tracks apply instead. Cases inside the 180-to-210-day statutory window have not yet matured (outer edge: at least 210 days from final disposition).
Federal record holders and out-of-state agencies are excluded: North Carolina expunction does not reach them.
The participant obtains a right-to-review copy of their own SBI criminal history before the request goes out; LegalEase never sees it.
Fees: none for the request itself; a certificate of verification, where the holder requires one, may carry a clerk's fee.
The record holder's name and mailing address are participant-confirmed against the agency's own published contact details; never guessed.

Self-help ends if the holder refuses or does not respond — a second letter is not the answer and the participant needs a lawyer. Immigration matters: this correspondence should not go out without advice, because expunction can harm an immigration case by destroying record access.

correspondence.subjectLine: Request to conform agency records to an automatic expunction under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-146(a4)
bodyParagraphs: My name is {senderName}. I am writing about records your agency holds concerning me. According to my review, the following charge or charges still appear in your records: {chargesStillShowing}. I saw the charge still showing {whereSeen}.

This is my account of the case: the charge or charges arose in {countyAndFileNumber}, and the last charge reached its final disposition on {finalDispositionDate}. It is my understanding that those charges were expunged by operation of law under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-146(a4). I am not certifying the expunction myself; I am asking your agency to check its own records against the court's records.

By way of background: under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-146(a4), certain charges are expunged by operation of law, and the clerk is not required to transmit an expunction order to other entities, so your agency may never have received notice that the expunction occurred. N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-150 states the notification scheme for expunctions generally, and N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-153 restores a person whose record is expunged to the status they occupied before the arrest, charge or conviction.

I therefore respectfully request that your agency: (1) check its own records against the court's records for the case identified above; and (2) if that check confirms the expunction, conform your agency's records to it so the expunged charge or charges no longer appear.

If your agency requires written proof that the expunction occurred before it will act, please tell me in writing what proof you require. I understand the clerk of court offers an application process for a certificate of verification of a prior expunction, and I can pursue that process if you need it.
Please send your written response to my mailing address shown above. Thank you for your attention to this request.
enclosures: [COPY OF THE RELEVANT PAGE OF THE SENDER'S OWN RECORD CHECK OR BACKGROUND REPORT SHOWING THE CHARGE STILL APPEARING — SENDER ENCLOSES A COPY ONLY]

provenance.registryExcerpt: This supporting action produces the participant's own written request asking the record holder to conform its records to the expunction that has already happened. It seeks no new relief and asks no court for anything. Rules: nothing is filed with a court; the request is sent directly to the record holder by mail with proof of posting or the agency's published written channel; no fee for the request itself (a certificate of verification may carry a clerk's fee); no notice; no service ('This is correspondence, not a filing'); participant signs and dates; notarization none required. Packet instructions: the letter must not assert that the agency has broken any duty and must not certify that the expunction occurred; the participant obtains a right-to-review copy of their own SBI criminal history first. Conditional component: certificate_of_verification_application = official form AOC-G-260 (official_pdf_fill). Waiting period: at least 210 days from final disposition (outer edge of the automatic window). Exclusions: cases where the automatic expunction did not occur; the 180-210-day window not yet mature; federal and out-of-state holders; the court record itself (G.S. 15A-151(a1)).
